## What you do not need {#what-you-do-not-need-today}

::: {.none}
- No git, no GitHub account and no OSF account – we read the OSF from the outside, as any reader can
- Nothing more to install: the IDE workspace that you installed before the day holds every task, and you work in it, in your IDE
- These slides run R inside the browser and show each step with its output, so they carry the work if your installation fails
- Nothing leaves your machine except what you choose to send
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Do this now:** open the folder of the IDE workspace. If your installation failed, open these slides in a tab of your own instead, and leave them to load.
:::

::: notes
Today you need no git and no account with GitHub or the OSF, because we read the OSF from the outside, as any reader can, and you need to install nothing more. The IDE workspace that you installed before the day holds every task in its report, and that is where you work. These slides are what I drive on the shared screen, and since R runs inside them, in the browser, on each hands-on slide I run the step in front of you and you can compare my output with yours. If your installation has failed, open the slides in a tab of your own and work in their cells, or in the webR workspace on the workshop's website, which holds the same tasks as a page. [advance] One thing to do now, while I talk: open the folder of the IDE workspace.
:::
